title: Strictly positive integral grading of a sharp lattice monoid
statement: Let $G$ be a free abelian group of finite rank (a free $\mathbf Z$-module with finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]), meaning a group isomorphic to $\mathbf Z^r$ for some integer $r\ge0$. Let $P\subseteq G$ be an additive submonoid generated by a finite set, and assume $P\cap(-P)=\{0\}$. Then there is a group homomorphism $w:G\to\mathbf Z$ such that $w(p)>0$ for every $p\in P\setminus\{0\}$. Its restriction is an additive map $P\to\mathbf N$. The trivial monoid $P=\{0\}$ is allowed.

source.place: Agent-supplied convex-algebra refinement for the sharp fs monoids of VI 1.6, printed p. 70, and VIII 3.1.1, 3.1.10, printed pp. 98--99. Strict positivity is a rational cone separation input, not a theorem asserted verbatim in ILO.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating list $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ for $P$ and embed $G$ into $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ using a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis. Let $C$ be the cone generated by the images $p_j\otimes1$. If $x\in C\cap(-C)$, clear the finitely many rational denominators in expressions for $x$ and $-x$ to obtain $a,b\in P$ and an integer $N>0$ with $Nx=a\otimes1$ and $-Nx=b\otimes1$. Then $(a+b)\otimes1=0$, hence $a+b=0$ in the embedded group. Thus $a\in P\cap(-P)$, so $a=b=0$ and $x=0$. Therefore $C$ is pointed.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103; denominator-clearing and sharpness argument supplied here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite] to the finite-dimensional rational vector space $V$ and the generators $p_j\otimes1$. It gives finitely many rational linear forms $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s$ such that $C=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge0\text{ for all }i\}$. Set $\lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$. For $c\in C$ all summands are nonnegative. If $\lambda(c)=0$, every $\lambda_i(c)=0$, so every $\lambda_i(-c)=0$ and $-c\in C$. Pointedness from Step 1 then gives $c=0$. Thus $\lambda(c)>0$ for every nonzero $c\in C$. This includes an empty family: then $C=V$, and pointedness forces $V=0$, so $\lambda=0$ suffices.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103 is motivating context only. The finite rational half-space description is the cited DAG statement (its Kato 1994 source remains WANTED); summing the defining forms and using pointedness is the elementary agent-supplied argument written here.

proof.text: Choose the finite $\mathbf Z$-basis of $G$ from the hypothesis. The values of $\lambda$ on its basis vectors are rational; multiply $\lambda$ by a common positive denominator $d$ so that $w(g):=d\lambda(g\otimes1)$ is an integer for every $g\in G$. Then $w:G\to\mathbf Z$ is a group homomorphism, and for every $p\in P\setminus\{0\}$ its image in $V$ is a nonzero element of $C$, so $w(p)=d\lambda(p\otimes1)>0$.

source.place: Agent-supplied lattice-coordinate denominator-clearing argument following Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103.

proof.text: For $p\in P$, positivity gives $w(p)\in\mathbf N$, and additivity of $w$ restricts to an additive map $P\to\mathbf N$. The case $P=\{0\}$ has no nonzero element and is already covered (one may take $w=0$).

source.place: Agent-supplied final restriction argument; Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103.
